cards.explanation: The answer is after they enter the land He's giving them. The LORD says, “After you enter the land that I am giving you as a home” (Numbers 15:2). Notice He's already talking about a home they haven't reached yet. I know a little about waiting for a new place, so I like hearing it, friends.

The answer is exactly as the Israelites do. The text says the foreigner “…is to do exactly as you do.” (Numbers 15:14). No side door, friends, and no special version. If you're bringing it, you're bringing it the same way.

The word is permanent. The LORD says, “it is a permanent statute for the generations to come.” (Numbers 15:15). He adds, “You and the foreigner shall be the same before the LORD.” One law for everyone, friends, and it stays.

The answer is the first of their dough. The LORD says, “From the first of your dough, you are to lift up a cake as a contribution…” (Numbers 15:20). Of everything in this passage, friends, this is the one that gets my mustache twitching. A cake from the first of the dough goes to Him.

The answer is False. This is not a one-time gift for their first harvest. The LORD says, “Throughout your generations, you are to give the LORD an offering from the first of your dough.” (Numbers 15:21). It's not a one-and-done, friends. Every generation gives from the first of its dough.

The answer is one young bull and one male goat. The whole congregation is to prepare “…one young bull as a burnt offering…” with its grain offering and drink offering, “…and one male goat as a sin offering.” (Numbers 15:24). One bull, one goat, friends. Easy to count, hard to forget.

The word is forgiven. The text says the priest makes atonement “…so that they may be forgiven; for the sin was unintentional…” (Numbers 15:25). The congregation brings a food offering and a sin offering, and the priest makes atonement for them. Then the text adds, “Then the whole congregation of Israel and the foreigners residing among them will be forgiven…” (Numbers 15:26). That's good news, friends, and I'll take it every time.

The answer is True. The text says, “Then the whole congregation of Israel and the foreigners residing among them will be forgiven, since it happened to all the people unintentionally.” (Numbers 15:26). The foreigners are named right in the verse, friends. Nobody is left standing at the door.

The answer is a year-old female goat. The text says, “…if one person sins unintentionally, he is to present a year-old female goat as a sin offering.” (Numbers 15:27). The congregation's sin offering is a goat too, friends, but a male one (Numbers 15:24). For one person, it's a year-old female goat.

The answer is False. The foreigner does not follow a different law. The LORD says, “You shall have the same law for the one who acts in error, whether he is a native-born Israelite or a foreigner residing among you.” (Numbers 15:29). One law covers both, friends. No second rulebook.

The answer is that he blasphemes the LORD. The text says, “But the person who sins defiantly, whether a native or foreigner, blasphemes the LORD.” (Numbers 15:30). This is a heavy part, friends. The text treats defiance very differently from an accident.

The answer is False. The text says the defiant person “…shall be cut off from among his people.” (Numbers 15:30). It ends with “his guilt remains on him.” (Numbers 15:31). The passage gives atonement and forgiveness to the one who strayed unintentionally, friends (Numbers 15:28).

The answer is that he despised the word of the LORD. The text says, “He shall certainly be cut off, because he has despised the word of the LORD and broken His commandment…” (Numbers 15:31). Two things are named there, friends: despising the word of the LORD and breaking His commandment. The verse then ends with “his guilt remains on him.” (Numbers 15:31).
